newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian financial information highway to launch Nov 6.
newsitem.headline: Belgian financial information highway to launch Nov 6.

text.p: An electronic banking and communications network backed by seven Belgian banks will be launched on November 6 and so far has 4,000 prospective clients, the project's management said on Tuesday.

Isabel -- Interbank Standards Association Belgium -- will be an information highway for financial communication. Its services include secure electronic banking with 30 member banks, electronic mail, and access to news providers and the Internet.
"At the moment we have 140 customers installed, and from January we will be installing about 2,000 a month" Philippe Dubois, Isabel's managing director, told a news conference.
So far 4,000 customers had signed contracts, said Jean-Francois de le Court, a member of Banque Bruxelles Lambert (BBL).
BBL is one of Isabel's shareholders with BACOB Bank, CGER Bank, Credit Communal de Belgique, CERA Bank, Generale Bank and Kredietbank/Credit General.
"Our primary aim is to have a system which is effective, flexible, secure and good value," De le Court said, adding that for now Isabel was targetting companies, not individuals.
Isabel's main business would be electronic banking, with other services offering added value. The aim was not to compete with other access providers.

The core multibank services will cost a basic 400 Belgian francs a month plus charges for network use, or 1,150 francs a month all in. Communications services are charged at an additional 750 francs a month, and off-line services 100 francs.

Dubois said Isabel's business plan foresaw break-even three years after its launch on turnover of two billion francs. However, he emphasised the plan was drawn up two years ago when the Internet was much less known.

With an estimated 1,500 billion francs swilling round its system every year, Isabel promises security and confidentiality by the use of "smart card" technology based on clients having two codes - a public and a private one. Clients will be able to use a single password for all the banks.

Isabel offers access to a standardised platform and will allow an exchange of information not only between banks and companies but companies themselves and also companies and their commercial partners, the association said.
